deep.reconstruction:
Context: the manuscript bundle traces rays through a two-lens achromatic objective. The lens is a crown lens followed by a flint lens, in contact at the vertex. The previous page traces an oblique ray (1 degree) exactly with logarithms and gets an intersection distance of 2417.538. The next page traces a marginal ray exactly and gets 2418.643. It also compares the result with values labelled Fraunhofer, Klügel and Bohnenberger. This page does the paraxial (Gaussian) calculation of the same objective for violet rays ('Violette Strahlen'). It uses the alpha, beta, gamma, delta coefficients of Gauss's Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841).

(1) Data (logarithms; 'n' marks a negative number).
- Refractive indices: n1 = 1.536071 (crown) and n2 = 1.65926884 (flint). Their logs are 0.1864113 and 0.2199167 (last line).
- Row 1: log(n1-1) = 9.7292223 and log(n2-1) = 9.8190625.
- Radii, crown: log r1 = 3.2538828, so |r1| = 1794.25; log r2 = 2.8539990, so |r2| = 714.4946.
- Radii, flint: log r3 = 2.8624520n, so r3 = -728.5377; log r4 = 3.3901415, so |r4| = 2455.533. The same radii appear on the previous page.
- Thicknesses: log t1 = 1.1430148, so t1 = 13.9 (crown); log t2 = 1.0334238, so t2 = 10.8 (flint).
- The air gap between the lenses is zero.

(2) Elements of the system [names mine]:
- surface powers: p1 = (n1-1)/r1 = beta = +0.0002987717 (log 6.4753395); f' = (n1-1)/|r2| = +0.00075028 (log 6.8752233); f'' = (n2-1)/r3 = -0.00090496 (log 6.9566105n); f''' = (n2-1)/|r4| = +0.00026848 (log 6.4289210);
- reduced thicknesses: h = t1/n1 = 9.049060 (log 0.9566035); h'' = t2/n2 = 6.50886 (log 0.8135071); h' = 0 for the air gap.

(3) Recursion. Gauss builds the sequence alpha, beta, alpha', beta', ... with the rule X_k = -X_{k-2} + X_{k-1}*e_k, where e_k runs through h, f', h' = 0, f'', h'', f'''. Each boxed pair on the page is the product X_{k-1}*e_k (by logarithms) added to -X_{k-2}.
- alpha = 1.
- alpha' = -1 + beta*h = -1 + 0.002703604 = -0.997296396.
- beta' = -beta + alpha'*f' = -0.0002987717 - 0.0007482516 = -0.0010470233.
- alpha'' = -alpha' + beta'*0 = +0.997296396.
- beta'' = -beta' + alpha''*f'' = 0.0010470233 - 0.0009024742 = +0.0001445493.
- alpha''' = -alpha'' + beta''*h'' = -0.997296396 + 0.000940856 = -0.996355540.
- beta''' = -beta'' + alpha'''*f''' = -0.0001445493 - 0.0002675072 = -0.0004120565 (log 6.6149568).
- Second chain, starting from gamma = 0, delta = 1:
  - gamma' = h = 9.049060.
  - delta' = -1 + gamma'*f' = -1 + 0.006789331 = -0.993210669.
  - gamma'' = -gamma' = -9.049060.
  - delta'' = -delta' + gamma''*f'' = 0.993210669 + 0.008188681 = +1.001399350.
  - gamma''' = -gamma'' + delta''*h'' = 9.049060 + 6.517997 = 15.567057.
  - delta''' = -delta'' + gamma'''*f''' = -1.001399350 + 0.004179531 = -0.997219819.

(4) Result: 2418.007 = -alpha'''/beta''' = 0.99635554/0.0004120565.
- This is the paraxial back focal distance (from the last vertex) for parallel violet light.
- It is compared with the exact traces on the neighbouring pages (2417.538 oblique, 2418.643 marginal), i.e. a study of spherical and field aberration.
- [Mine] 1/|beta'''| = 2426.85 is the equivalent focal length.
- [Mine] The final coefficients satisfy alpha'''*delta''' - beta'''*gamma''' = 1, as Gauss's theory requires.
errors: delta''' is written '0,99721 9819' without a sign. The page's own computation (-1.00139935 + 0.004179531) gives delta''' = -0.997219819; the minus sign is omitted.
log f' is written 6.8752233 in the first block and 6.8752235 in the second block. The correct value is 9.7292223 - 2.8539990 = 6.8752233; the discrepancy is negligible.
No other errors found; all checked products and sums agree to the 7-8 digits carried.

results.what: Paraxial imaging through a 4-surface cemented-contact achromat computed by the recursive alpha/beta/gamma/delta coefficient scheme (continuant with alternating signs) using surface powers (n-1)/r and reduced thicknesses t/n
results.modern_name: Gaussian optics / ray-transfer (ABCD) matrix method; Gaussian brackets (continuants)
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841); matrix form later (Sampson 1913 etc.)

results.what: Paraxial back focal distance for violet rays, 2418.007 = -alpha'''/beta''', compared with exact trigonometric ray traces (2417.538, 2418.643) to assess aberrations of a Fraunhofer-type objective
results.modern_name: Back focal distance; longitudinal spherical/chromatic aberration evaluation
results.usually_credited_to: Standard lens design practice (Fraunhofer, Gauss, Seidel era)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked application of Gauss's own published 1841 paraxial coefficient method to an achromatic objective. It is of archival interest only.
